verdicts.evidence: Dropping the `^` lets any `---\n...\n---` block ANYWHERE in a rule file be read as frontmatter, and this parser feeds the ASI coverage of every artefact in the pack. Probed two reachable missions: (a) a house rule whose file opens with a UTF-8 BOM - shipped build ignores its frontmatter, mutant counts it, ASI03 gains `house-bom`; (b) a rule file with no frontmatter that quotes an example one in its body - the mutant reads `asi: [ASI05, ASI07]` out of the prose and adds `house-doc` to two categories that the corpus does not actually cover there. Coverage inflated from a sentence in a body is the pack overstating what addresses a risk. Both are legitimate missions: corpusDivergence explicitly allows house rules ('extend freely'). It is also a divergence between two layers reading one file: the gate's own parsers (rules.ts:58, conformance.ts:33) keep the anchor, so `check` and the pack would disagree about the same rule - the RWD-2026-0061 shape. Nothing notices: no fixture has a rule file whose frontmatter is not at byte 0.
